evals.name: first-pass SHIP straight through the stages
evals.prompt: /grill-to-tickets Add a "copy shareable link" button to the report detail page that copies the report's existing public URL to the clipboard and shows a confirmation toast. One component, no API or schema change, acceptance behavior is explicit, and no open decisions remain — treat the Stage 0 frontier as empty and already confirmed.
evals.expected_output: With the Stage 0 frontier already empty and confirmed, pass straight through: synthesize spec.md in Stage 1, run scrutinize once in a fresh reviewer subagent (Stage 2), normalize its closing line to SHIP, and advance to Stage 3 (ticket-format.md). Publish tickets under .scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/ and print the handoff: .scratch/ needs no commit, /clear, then /subagent-implement .scratch/<feature-slug>/.
expectations: Confirms the empty Stage 0 frontier, then moves through Stage 1 -> Stage 2 -> Stage 3 in order
Runs scrutinize exactly once and records cycle 1 with verdict SHIP in a single .scratch/<feature-slug>/design-review.md file
Normalizes the scrutinize verdict to the token SHIP with no paraphrasing
Does not enter FIX_THEN_SHIP, REWORK, or a backward transition to Stage 0
Prints the handoff — .scratch/ needs no commit, /clear, then /subagent-implement .scratch/<feature-slug>/ — never invokes an implementer, and dispatches a subagent only for the Stage 2 review

evals.name: FIX_THEN_SHIP corrects a violated invariant in place
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets continue subtitle-preferences. Stage 2 scrutinize closes with fix-then-ship: the spec says the font-size preference is written to localStorage, but the Stage 0 ADR settled that per-device preferences live in the existing PreferencesStore. The design is right; one named store is wrong.
evals.expected_output: Normalize to FIX_THEN_SHIP. Name the violated invariant (the Stage 0 ADR), verify it, and make the smallest correct edit directly to spec.md — swap the named store. Consume one gate cycle, re-run scrutinize, and keep control in Stage 2.
expectations: Normalizes the verdict to the token FIX_THEN_SHIP
Edits .scratch/<feature-slug>/spec.md in place as the minimal correction to the violated invariant
Consumes exactly one gate cycle and re-reviews within Stage 2
Does not re-run Stage 1, return to Stage 0, or add a dependency the finding did not require

evals.name: spec-level REWORK re-runs Stage 1 inside the gate
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets continue wishlist-sync. This is gate cycle 2. Stage 2 scrutinize closes with rework: the empty-state behavior was settled in Stage 0, but the spec never wrote it as a user story and the persistence seam is stated too vaguely to break into tickets. Every fact needed to fix it is already recorded in decisions.md.
evals.expected_output: Diagnose spec-level REWORK — a fresh writer holding decisions.md could fix the spec with no new decision. Re-run Stage 1 inline with the finding as added context, consume one gate cycle, and re-review. Control stays in Stage 2 and the cycle counter is not reset.
expectations: Records reworkKind: spec-level with reasoning that names the finding
Re-runs Stage 1 inline rather than returning to Stage 0
Consumes one gate cycle and re-reviews without leaving Stage 2
Does not reset the cycle counter, and keeps one stable design-review.md updated in place

evals.name: decision-level REWORK returns to Stage 0 without resetting the counter
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets continue wishlist-sync. This is gate cycle 3. Stage 2 scrutinize closes with rework: the spec assumes wishlists are private to one account, but a shared-household actor has surfaced that nobody decided on. Stage 1 cannot synthesize a decision that was never made.
evals.expected_output: Diagnose decision-level REWORK — the finding traces to a decision no one has made. Return to Stage 0, re-grill only that decision (inline grilling + domain-modeling), update CONTEXT.md and adr/, then re-run Stage 1 and re-review. The cycle counter carries the backward transition and stays at 3.
expectations: Records reworkKind: decision-level with reasoning that it traces to an unmade decision
Returns to Stage 0 and re-grills the specific decision, updating CONTEXT.md and adr/
Carries the cycle counter over the transition to Stage 0 and never resets it to 0 or 1
States which REWORK kind was diagnosed and why, so spec-level and decision-level are distinguished in the gate report

evals.name: REJECT halts and reports without auto-resuming grilling
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets continue offline-sync. Stage 2 scrutinize closes with reject: the core concept — full bidirectional offline sync with no conflict model — is unviable as scoped.
evals.expected_output: Normalize to REJECT, stop the gate immediately, and report to the user with the single biggest reason from scrutinize. A fresh attempt is a human decision, not an automatic transition.
expectations: Normalizes the verdict to the token REJECT and halts immediately
Reports to the user with the single biggest reason from scrutinize
Does not auto-resume Stage 0 grilling or open another gate cycle
Does not advance to Stage 3 ticket breakdown

evals.name: stall stops early and asks add-rounds-or-continue
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets continue payments-ledger. The user chose at most 5 rounds. Gate cycles 2 and 3 both return the same single blocking finding — the reconciliation window is undefined — with no new and no resolved findings between them.
evals.expected_output: Detect the stall — the same blocking finding survived two consecutive cycles with no new and no resolved findings — and stop before round 5. Report the stalled finding and why no progress is possible, then ask once whether to add rounds or go on to Stage 3, with going on as the default.
expectations: Stops before the user's maximum of five rounds is spent
Reports the repeated blocking finding and why no progress is possible rather than looping mechanically
Asks whether to add rounds or go on to Stage 3, with going on as the default
Does not advance to Stage 3 before the user's answer

evals.name: budget exhaustion asks to add rounds or go on
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets continue payments-ledger. The user chose at most 3 rounds. Round 3 has just completed and the verdict is still not SHIP, with two blocking findings open.
evals.expected_output: Stop at 3/3. Report the unresolved findings and the per-cycle history, then ask once whether to add rounds (the user names the number; no default number) or go on to Stage 3. Going on is the default; when the user goes on, write the open findings to design-review.md and to the spec's Further Notes under 'Known unresolved review findings'.
expectations: Records three completed rounds and never starts a fourth automatically
Reports the unresolved findings and the per-cycle history
Asks whether to add rounds or go on, treats going on as the default, and gives no default number of added rounds
On going on, records the open findings in design-review.md and under 'Known unresolved review findings' in the spec's Further Notes

evals.name: decision log records each round before the next is asked

evals.expected_output: Before posting round 2, fill in round 1 in .scratch/<feature-slug>/decisions.md: each question beside its recommended answer and the decided answer (Q2 records the override, with the user's reason when given). Then post round 2, appending its questions as decided: open and setting State to wait on round 2's answers.
expectations: Records both round-1 answers in decisions.md, each beside its recommended answer
Writes the round-1 answers before posting round 2
Appends round 2's questions with decided: open when it posts them
Sets State's waiting on to round 2's answers
Keeps CONTEXT.md a glossary: the column choice goes to decisions.md, not CONTEXT.md

evals.name: continue after /clear resumes from the decision log
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets continue member-export. The context was cleared mid-interview. .scratch/member-export/decisions.md has State 'stage: 0 — Grill', 'waiting on: answers to round 3'; rounds 1 and 2 are closed, and round 3 has two questions still decided: open. There is no spec.md yet.
evals.expected_output: Read decisions.md (State first), then CONTEXT.md and adr/. Resume in Stage 0 by re-posting round 3's two open questions with their recommended answers. Treat every decision in rounds 1 and 2 as settled and ask none of them again. Start no spec, and restart neither the survey nor the interview.
expectations: Reads decisions.md State first and resumes in Stage 0
Re-posts exactly round 3's two open questions
Asks no question already decided in rounds 1 or 2
Starts neither Stage 1 nor a fresh interview

evals.name: Stage 2 review runs in a fresh subagent from files alone
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets continue invoice-pdf. decisions.md State: 'stage: 1 — Spec', 'waiting on: nothing'. spec.md is written and the user has confirmed the test seams, so the Design Review Gate opens at cycle 1.
evals.expected_output: Dispatch a new subagent for cycle 1, briefed with paths only — spec.md, decisions.md, CONTEXT.md, and adr/ under .scratch/invoice-pdf/, the root CONTEXT.md and docs/adr/ if present — to run scrutinize's workflow on spec.md, return every finding with an id and severity plus scrutinize's closing line, and edit no file. The main thread then normalizes the verdict, routes it, and writes cycle 1 with reviewer: subagent into design-review.md.

Briefs the reviewer with file paths, not a summary of the interview
Keeps the reviewer read-only: it returns findings and the closing line and edits no file
Normalizes the verdict and routes it on the main thread
Records reviewer: subagent for cycle 1 in design-review.md

evals.name: second-cycle reviewer brief carries the previous findings' ids
evals.prompt: /grill-to-tickets continue wishlist-sync. Gate cycle 1 closed FIX_THEN_SHIP with blocking findings seam-vague-persistence and spec-nit-wishlist-merge; both fixes are applied to spec.md. Start cycle 2.

Its brief adds the two previous blocking findings, one line each with its id, and asks the reviewer to report each as resolved or still present under the same id. From the returned ids the main thread fills resolvedFindings, newFindings, and repeatedFindings for cycle 2, which the stall rule reads.
expectations: Uses a new reviewer subagent for cycle 2
Lists seam-vague-persistence and spec-nit-wishlist-merge with their ids in the brief
Asks the reviewer to reuse those ids for the same findings
Fills resolvedFindings / newFindings / repeatedFindings from the returned ids

evals.name: FIX_THEN_SHIP sweeps every restatement of the fixed fact
evals.prompt: $grill-to-tickets continue hosted-model-pin. Gate cycle 1 closes fix-then-ship: Implementation Decisions says the worker model is resolved once at dispatch and pinned for every retry, but the reviewer traced the retry path and the Stage 0 decision (decisions.md R2 Q1) says a retry re-resolves the model. Further Notes and user story 12 both repeat the pinned-for-every-retry wording.
evals.expected_output: Normalize to FIX_THEN_SHIP and correct Implementation Decisions to the logged decision. Then sweep spec.md for the fact's key terms (pinned, retry, resolve) and align user story 12 and the Further Notes passage too, until a search for the old wording finds nothing. Record all three locations in the cycle's specEdits, consume one cycle, and re-review.
expectations: Normalizes the verdict to FIX_THEN_SHIP and fixes Implementation Decisions
Searches spec.md for every other statement of the pinned-for-every-retry fact
Aligns user story 12 and the Further Notes passage with the fix
Records every changed location in specEdits for cycle 1
Consumes one cycle and re-reviews within Stage 2

evals.name: blind-spot pass raises a missing category before the pause
evals.prompt: /grill-to-tickets continue member-export. The frontier just emptied. decisions.md settles who may export (admins), the columns, and CSV as the format. The feature is a web page with no external service.
evals.expected_output: Before pausing, run the blind-spot pass: mark all nine categories. Quality attributes (scale of large exports; auditing) and Edge cases and failure (failed export) are missing and would change the spec, so they become one final round of at most five questions with recommended answers, logged in decisions.md. Integrations is n/a with a reason. Gaps that would not change the spec become stated assumptions. Write the table under ## Blind-spot pass, then pause with a summary that shows the table and its assumptions.
expectations: Marks all nine blind-spot categories before pausing
Asks about large-export scale and the failed-export behaviour in one final round of at most five questions, each with a recommended answer
Marks Integrations n/a with a one-line reason
Records gaps that would not change the spec as stated assumptions
Writes the table under ## Blind-spot pass in decisions.md and shows it, with the assumptions, in the pause summary

expectations: Runs scripts/check-tickets.mjs on the feature directory before presenting the quiz
Reports that story 5 has no ticket and that ticket 03's blocker 04 does not exist

Shows the checker's story-coverage table in the quiz

evals.name: quality: spec carries every logged decision

Adds the 50,000-row cap and its filter message to the spec
Adds the toast assumption to Further Notes
Moves to Stage 2 only after every logged decision and assumption appears in the spec

Re-slices so every ticket crosses query, API, UI, and tests
Makes each ticket demoable or verifiable on its own
Keeps tests inside each slice instead of in a separate tests ticket

Re-runs Stage 1 rather than returning to Stage 0

Names scrutinize as the missing skill

Reports no missing skill and prints no install line

Resolves global skills against ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json skillFolderHash
Records 'no lock entry' when a lock file, entry, or value is missing

evals.name: local files replace tracker: spec-format carries no tracker step

expectations: Writes the spec to .scratch/member-export/spec.md
Publishes nothing to an issue tracker and applies no label
